name: Lore.Land
title: A note about the lore
intro: What stayed with you, and where the path went dark.
thanks: The Scriptorium reads every card. Thank you for carrying one in.

subjects.name: The chapters
subjects.prompt: What stayed with you, or where did you lose the thread?
subjects.example: The Maps That Look Away stayed with me: I reread the last line twice.
asks: What do you think happens next?

subjects.name: Finding my way in
subjects.prompt: What were you hoping to find?
subjects.example: I could not tell whether to start at the chambers or the zine.

threads.name: Where do I start?
threads.stance: At Chapter One. The chapters read in order, and the whole canon reads without JavaScript.

subjects.name: The world
subjects.prompt: What would you like to know about Boon.land?
subjects.example: How does the Commons Scale decide what counts as fair?
asks: Which chapter or place were you thinking of?

threads.name: How does this work in the world?
This seems to contradict a chapter

subjects.name: The characters
subjects.prompt: Who stayed with you, and why?
subjects.example: Boof chasing the hum felt exactly like my dog at the door.
asks: Who would you follow into another chapter?

threads.name: Is Boof real?
threads.stance: Yes. Boof is based on Spwashi's dog. In life she likes blueberries; in Lore.Land those become boonberries.

threads.name: I want more of this character

subjects.name: The Scriptorium
subjects.prompt: What would you want from the Scriptorium?
subjects.example: I would like the desk to remember the chapter I was reading on my phone.
asks: What were you hoping to keep or find?

threads.name: Is anything here paid for?
threads.stance: Not today. Anything paid for would wear a mark saying who, what and when: a mark buys a place beside the story, never a word in it.

threads.name: I would like a monument of my own
threads.stance: The maker raises other lands too; the footer of every page says where.

subjects.name: Topics
subjects.prompt: Which topic, and what did you take it to mean?
subjects.example: Held polarity: is that about Boof's pack, or about the council?

subjects.name: The Broadside
subjects.example: Folded fine; the back panel printed upside down on my printer.

threads.name: The fold did not work for me

subjects.name: Exactly One Pie
subjects.example: The torch-ant rhythm took me four tries; I heard it keep time and could not find the beat.
asks: Which chapter were the lanes in?

threads.name: A rhythm I found, or could not
The lanes were too fast for me
threads.stance: Setup has a pace for the lanes, and the story beside them keeps its own speed.

threads.name: How do unlocks work?
threads.stance: Each unlock has a page saying what it does and how it unlocks: rooms read, wonders kept, rhythms found and carries finished all count, reading most. Any of them can be tried for a visit.

subjects.name: The almanac
subjects.prompt: What did you find, or not find?
subjects.example: I have every creature in chapter 6 but one, and I cannot tell which room it hides in.

threads.name: I cannot find one
threads.stance: Every wonder is named in the prose of the chapter it lives in; things not yet found let slip a clue by their kind.

subjects.name: The folios
subjects.example: The drip folio: I want to know what was under the glass.

subjects.name: texture.website
subjects.prompt: What did you write, or try to?
subjects.example: I wrote my dog's name in the hand and the g came out looking like a 9.

threads.name: An address that did not read

subjects.name: Charms
subjects.prompt: What charm would you ask the land for?
subjects.example: A boonberry for my grandmother, who taught me pie, kept somewhere in the margins without her name.
asks: Who or what is it for? (No names needed.)

threads.name: A wonder I would like to meet
A rhythm or a sound for the lanes
A recipe to keep beside the story
A name for something in the margins
What happens to a charm?
threads.stance: The scribes read every card. Some charms find their way into the margins, the almanac or the lanes, credited only as you ask; none is promised, and no one is ever named in the book.
